correctness.rationale: Rebuilt determinant Δ=m(m+2)-1 and inverse (u,v) coordinates for a primitive line direction w=(a,b). If b≠0 the integer identity m[(m+2)b-a]+(ma-b)=Δb forces max absolute numerator>=m+1, bounding nonhorizontal primitive length by nΔ/(m+1), strictly >1 below the continuous horizontal bound nΔ/m. In the middle horizontal strip y∈[n,mn], endpoints give ℓ(y)=n(m+2)-p-1_(y mod m<t)-1_(y mod m>0). Outer integral-height strips have shorter chords. Counting exactly the admissible residues gives both branches and pairwise distinct residue slopes; a supposed smaller quasiperiod would identify two different slopes. Independently enumerated all lattice points and all maximal pair gcd-directions for 16 configurations 2<=m<=5,1<=n<=4; all lengths, horizontal uniqueness and counts agree. Enumeration corroborates only bounded cases; proof gives the infinite m,n result.
residual_risks: Maximal lattice-diameter segments are counted once per supporting lattice line and not by arbitrary subsegments.
m=3 special case is already published; the present formula correctly reduces to that case.

evidence: Theorem4.6 covers eventual quasipolynomiality of segment counts for every fixed lattice polytope, but does not bound or realize least periods.

value.rationale: Shows a qualitatively unbounded arithmetic phenomenon within the simplest centrally symmetric lattice polygons: four primitive edges suffice for any prescribed least quasiperiod and an m-fold spectrum of growth slopes. This supplies explicit realizability and strong nonuniformity examples beyond a fixed isolated table computation.
residual_risks: No claim of classification for arbitrary polygons or coordinate-optimality of construction.

final_claim: For every integer m>=2, the primitive-edged parallelogram spanned by (1,m),(m+2,1) has horizontal-only maximizing diameter segments of nP_m; writing n=mp+t, count n-p+1 if t=0 or (m-t+1)(n-p) if t>0, least eventual quasiperiod exactly m, m distinct leading slopes with max/min ratio m.
